clauses.reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; the table lists 10314 with a subject line describing an emergency board to investigate an airline labor dispute. The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer); this is not an until-date, so no inclusive or exclusive reading arises. The thirty-day report deadline and the statutory period after the report are not ends; the board's report is dated February 16, 1952 (held report title page), after which the order was functionally spent but remained on the books until this revocation (owner ruling 2026-10-21). No earlier end is shown in held evidence.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10314 at 16 FR 12709, in the Federal Register of December 19, 1951 (PDF page 1; govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified, recorded as acceptable as original). The order is headed Executive Order 10314 and is signed December 17, 1951. Text: the order recites a dispute between the Pan American World Airways, Inc., a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the Transport Workers Union of America, CIO; invoking section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, it creates a board of three members, to be appointed by the President, to investigate the dispute, and provides that no member may be pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of employees or any carrier. It directs that "The board shall report its findings to the President with respect to the said dispute within thirty days from the date of this order."; requires the board, in performing its functions, to comply with the requirements of section 502 of the Defense Production Act of 1950, as amended; and, as provided by section 10 of the Act, states that from the date of the order and for thirty days after the board has reported "no change, except by agreement, shall be made" by the company or its employees in the conditions out of which the dispute arose. Inventory: one whole-order clause, from the heading through the last operative sentence, confirmed against the held text. Ending: Executive Order 12553, headed "Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986" and printed at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986 (held govinfo text layer), orders that "the following Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked"; its No. Subject table lists 10314 with the subject "Creating an emergency board to investigate an airline labor dispute". The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording, so the revocation is dated on signing, 1986-02-25; this is a reading, disclosed for the reviewer, and the publication date of March 3, 1986 is not used. The enacting sentence has no exception or saving clause. Report: the held National Mediation Board copy of the board's report (source-ladder text for this order) is titled as the report of the emergency board appointed on January 9, 1952 pursuant to Executive Order 10314, and its title page is dated at New York, February 16, 1952; the report states that the parties stipulated to extend the time for the report to February 18, 1952 and that the President approved the extension. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, the report date and the end of any statutory period are spent facts: the order was functionally spent once the board had reported, but it remained on the books until its express revocation. Searches: I read the coverage notes of the three machine searches before selecting them. The U.S. Code search covers the release point current through 2026-10-09 (laws enacted from then through 2026-10-14 are not reflected) and the eCFR search runs as of 2026-10-14; both are complete with no coverage warning and serve here to show that no current provision gives this order continuing force after its revocation. The OFR disposition-note search records only the Executive Order 12553 revocation for this order. The held-text number search found this number only in the front matter of the board's report.
